Both Run proofs green, both freeze Checks green, and I exercised all five M1/M2 legs by hand against stub curl/git (factory present -> prints `factory` + the comment and logs the factory path, sandbox-boot.sh never run; factory absent -> `legacy` and the old log line; exactly one curl to /comment; `bash fleet-bootstrap.sh 9` against run=7 exits 1 with `refusing`; no engine= exits 1; a pre-existing engines/<sha> logs `already present` and never calls git). Two decisions a later session would otherwise rediscover:

1. `[ -f "$dst/factory/boot.sh" ] && boot=...` is safe under the file's `set -euo pipefail`. Bash exempts a non-final command of an AND-OR list from errexit, so the absent-factory case falls through to the default instead of exiting 1. Verified directly. Do not "fix" it into an if-block on suspicion; it costs bytes (see 2).

2. Byte budget is the real constraint on this file, not line count. At BASE renderSetupScript was 9028/9216 — 188 bytes of headroom for the whole edit. My first draft carried a two-line comment and landed at 9214, i.e. 2 bytes spare: passing, but it would have made the next byte anyone adds to either fleet-bootstrap.sh or setup-script.mjs fail the render. I cut the comment to one line; it now renders 9159, 57 bytes spare. Anyone touching this file should re-measure, and treat a sub-20-byte margin as a defect even though M3 only asks for <= budget.

exam for task 2 (the bootstrap's factory branch), approach before writing:

The exam lands at `fleet/tests/exams/run_187/test_fleet_bootstrap.mjs` (EXAM PATHS maps the Proof's `fleet/tests/test_fleet_bootstrap.mjs` there), so every relative path in it is written for that directory: `../../_helpers.mjs` for `simEnv` and `../../../` for `fleet/` itself (that `../../`-shaped helper import is also what `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs`'s `importerFor` resolves for an exam under `exams/<slug>/`, which is how the sweep reads the env through to `simEnv`).

Four spawns of `bash <fleet/fleet-bootstrap.sh>`, one per case, each with its own home and its own stub bin first on PATH, each `env: simEnv({ bin, home })`:

  1. factory — the `git` stub's `clone` writes BOTH `<dst>/factory/boot.sh` (0755, printing `factory` and $FLEET_ASSIGNMENT) and `<dst>/fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` (printing `legacy`, and touching a witness file before it prints).
  2. legacy — the same stub writes only `<dst>/fleet/sandbox-boot.sh`.
  3/4. the two refusals of M2 (`bash … 9` against a `run=7` comment; a comment with no `engine=`).
  5. already-present — `<FLEET_HOME>/engines/<sha>` pre-made with `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` in it, and the `git` stub's argv log asserted absent.

One reading worth writing down, because leg (a) does not spell it and a later session would have to reconstruct it: leg (a) asks that in the factory case `sandbox-boot.sh`'s stub was never run. For that to discriminate at all, the legacy stub has to EXIST and be runnable in the factory case — otherwise its silence only says the file was missing, not that the bootstrap chose the other path. So case 1's clone writes both stubs, the legacy one appends to a witness file as its first act, and the assertion is that the witness does not exist and no `legacy` line is on stdout. A mutant that keeps exec'ing sandbox-boot.sh is then red on the witness, not merely on a missing file.

Leg (c) [M3] is green at BASE by construction (the render is 9028 of 9216 bytes today, 188 bytes of headroom, and the task's own sketch of the change is ~110) — it is the budget guard for the edit, not the red leg. The red leg at BASE is (a)'s factory half: BASE's last two lines name `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` unconditionally, so stdout reads `legacy` where the leg asks `factory` and the log names the wrong exec path.

payload.body:
factory/boot.sh landed at 300 lines (the cap), `bash -n` clean, no `/usr/bin/` or `/usr/local/bin/` string in it, and both `git diff --quiet` freezes hold — the commit touches one file and adds 300 lines.

Shape: literals and one-line `fleet_*` wrappers for curl/git/npm/systemd-run/claude, every path off `$FLEET_HOME`; `json_field`/`json_int`/`json_escape` in grep+sed+awk (no jq, no python3); `prepare` (clone at base, plan-signature check, evidence worktree), `write_status` (thirteen cells, atomic), `ev_project` (one awk, `rows` for the PR table and `tasks` for the page), `evidence_commit` + `tick_events` (the relay), `auth_status` + `bearer_probe`, `run_engine` (the transient service), `publish`, `record_tags`, `boot`.

Deliberately dropped from the old boot: the status server and its port, the kata ping, merge, fold-again, the disclosures ticket, the residual reader, the card renderer, notify, the evidence lock and phase refresher, the public-github.com clone fallback, the gate-verdict blob reads, and enforcement of `tier`/`effort`/`hold` (accepted, ignored).

Smoked by hand against throwaway stubs (curl, git, npm, systemd-run, claude on PATH; the stub dir has been removed, nothing of it is in the tree) over seventeen legs: happy path; engine exit 1 with an answer -> draft PR + `parked`; engine exit 1 with no answer -> `failed`; head == base -> `parked` with zero POSTs; the four probe answers (200 alive, scope -> proceed, `"type":"error"` -> fail, `integration not found` -> fail, 418 -> inconclusive); `api_key` and no-token auth -> fail; unknown assignment key, bad base sha, and a moved plan branch -> fail; a 422 from the PR POST -> `error` is exactly the first 2000 characters and no tags are pushed; `ls-remote` disagreeing -> both branches kept, run still succeeds; the evidence push rejected -> five rebases per commit then local, run still opens the PR. The engine argv came out exactly `--plan --target --base --run-dir` with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=placeholder` as the only credential-shaped value, and the PR POST carried no `authorization` header.

One real bug the smoke caught and fixed before the commit: the first awk field extractor stopped at the first `"` in a quoted value, so a park reason quoting the exam (`the \"exam\" never went green`) both truncated and produced invalid JSON in `status.json`. The extractor now takes a quoted value with its JSON escapes intact and emits it back without re-escaping; `node -e JSON.parse` on the resulting page is clean and the reason survives whole.

payload.body: fix round 0, approach: both exam failures (ENGINE_FAILED and PR_REFUSED) are one bug in fail(). Its guard is `[ -e "$EVIDENCE_DIR/.git" ]` — a probe for "is there an evidence worktree to write into". A real `git worktree add` leaves a `.git` FILE there, so the guard held when I smoked it by hand against my own stubs; the peer exam's stub git answers `worktree add` with `mkdir -p "$dest"` and nothing else, so the guard is false and the failure page is never written — the boot logs `FAILED: …` and exits its code with status.json still reading `running`/`publishing`. The stub is not wrong to do that: nothing in the clause says the boot may depend on git internals to know it has a worktree. Fix: prepare() sets an EVIDENCE_READY flag on both its exits (fresh worktree and the retry case) and fail() guards on that flag instead of probing the filesystem for .git. No line-count change; the 300-line cap stays met.
